The petitioners have filed this claim petition U/Sec 166 of M.V. Act, 1989, against respondents seeking compensation on account of death of one Smt.Asim @ Naseema W/o Fayaz Ahmed, who died in Motor Vehicle Accident.

02. The brief facts of the case of the petitioners is as under:
On 16.03.2024 at about 02.00 a.m midnight, when said Asim @ Naseema was waiting for the bus on the left side of Bengaluru - Tumkur NH-48 Road, near JASS Toll India Oil Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala, at that time, the Lorry bearing No.TN-52-AB-9995 was also coming from Tumkur - Bengaluru Road and suddenly turned towards Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Bengaluru - Tumkur Road, without giving signal rashly and negligently with high speed and dashed against said Asim @
Naseema.
Due to impact, she fell down on the road and said lorry ran over her right leg and thus caused the accident.
Immediately after the accident she was shifted to Care Asia hospital, Nelamangala.
Inspite of best efforts made by the doctors, she succumbed to accidental injuries on the same day at 04.30 a.m.

The petitioners have spent Rs.1,00,000/-
(SCCH-3) 4 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 towards transportation and final rites etc.,.
Prior to accident the deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 47 years and was doing Mat vending business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m.

sentences.text:
The petitioner No.1 being husband,
petitioner No.2 being major son and petitioners No.3 and 4 are married daughters of the deceased.
The accident was occurred due to rash and negligent driving of offending Lorry and in this regard the Nelamangala Traffic Police have registered a case against driver of offending lorry.

The respondent No.1 being the owner and respondent No.2 being the insurer of offending lorry, are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation of Rs.26,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 12% p.a with costs.
03. Inspite of service of notice, the respondent No.1 did not appeared and hence was placed exparte.
On service of notice, the respondent No.2 has appeared before the tribunal through its counsel and filed objections.

04. The respondent No.2 in its objections has denied the entire case of the petitioners and further denied the alleged accident, negligence of the driver of (SCCH-3) 5 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 offending lorry, age, avocation and income of deceased and nature of the injuries sustained by the deceased and treatment taken by the deceased and expenses incurred by the petitioners.

Further, this respondent admits issuance of insurance policy with respect of offending lorry in favour of respondent No.1 and the liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy and contended that there is no valid permit and fitness certificate to the offending lorry and driver of lorry did not have driving licence to drive lorry as on the date of accident and hence there is breach of terms and conditions of the policy and the compensation claimed is highly excessive, exaggerated and hence,
pray to dismiss the petition with costs against respondent No.2.
05.

On the basis of the above pleadings of the parties, the following Issues has been framed by my learned predecessor:-
ISSUES

01 . Whether petitioners prove that they are only LR's/Dependents of deceased Asim @ Naseema W/o Fayaz Ahmed?
02. Whether petitioners prove that deceased Asim @ Naseema W/o Fayaz Ahmed was died in RTA rising out of the accident (SCCH-3) 6 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 alleged to have been taken place on 16.03.2024 at about 2:00 a.m, on Bengaluru- Tumakuru NH-48 Road, near Jass Toll Indian Oil Petrol Bunk, Nelamangala, Bengaluru Rural District, due to rash and negligent driving of Lorry bearing registration No. TN-52-AB-9995 by its driver as alleged in the petition?
03.
Whether petitioners are entitled for compensation?
If so, what amount & from whom?
04 . What order or award?

 REASONS  10. Issue No.1 :- Petitioner No.1 in his affidavit stated that, petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioners No.2 to 4 are the major son and married daughters of the deceased.
To prove the said facts, he has produced notarized copies of Aadhaar cards of himself, deceased and other petitioners as per Ex.P.9 to 13.
But as per the recent Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court even the major sons and married daughters are entitled to claim compensation for the death of their parents on all heads.
There is no dispute regarding dependency of the petitioners with the deceased.
These documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners are the legal heirs and dependents on the deceased.
Hence, I answered Issue No.1 in the Affirmative.
11. Issue No.2:- PW.1 filed affidavit by stating that due to the negligence of driver of the Lorry bearing No.TN-52-AB-9995 accident took place and deceased died in the accident.

Though, he has been elaborately cross-examined by the respondent No.2 counsel, but nothing is brought on record to disbelieve the case of (SCCH-3) 8 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 the petitioners that due to rash and negligent driving of the offending lorry by its driver, deceased sustained grievous injuries in the road traffic accident and later died.
On perusal of exhibited documents, Ex.P.1 FIR registered at Nelamangala Traffic Police against driver of offending lorry.
Ex.P.2 is the complaint which shows that due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending lorry the accident took place, in which the deceased sustained injuries and later died.

Ex.P.3 and 4 are the Spot Mahazar and Sketch shows the place of accident on Bengaluru - Tumkur Road, near Jass Toll Indian Oil Petrol Bunk,
Kasala Hobli, Nelamangala Taluk, which is not disputed.
Ex.P.5 is IMV report shows involvement of offending lorry in the accident.
Ex.P.6 is Inquest panchanama of the deceased Asim @ Naseema.
Ex.P.7 is Post mortem report of deceased Asim @ Naseema shows the cause of death is due to hypovolemic shock due to injury to long bone.

Accordingly, Issue No.2 is answered partly in the affirmative.
12. Issue No.3:- This issue is related to the entitlement of the compensation on account of the death of the deceased Asim @ Naseema, who died in the Motor Vehicle Accident.

The PW.1/petitioner No.1 has stated that prior to accident deceased was hale and healthy and was aged about 47 years and was doing Mat vending business and earning Rs.20,000/- p.m and have spent Rs.1,00,000/- towards transportation and final rites etc.,.

Due to untimely death of deceased,
the petitioners are put to great hardship and lost love and affection and dependency, loss of mental agony etc.,.
13. It is the duty of the petitioners to prove age of the deceased as on the date of accident.
The petitioners have not produced any birth certificate, school records or SSLC marks card of the deceased to show the exact date of birth of the deceased.
However, they have produced Ex.P.9 Aadhaar card of deceased.

Eventhough the said document is not authenticated document for the proof of age of any person, but in the absence of other evidence, said document can be relied upon and according to which her date of birth is mentioned as 01.01.1970.

The alleged accident (SCCH-3)
10 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 occurred on 16.03.2024 and hence it appears that as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased is 54 years.
Therefore, this tribunal has assessed the age of the deceased is 54 years as on the date of accident.

As per the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 in between Sarla Verma and Ors. V/s. Delhi Transport Corporation and Ors. case the multiplier applicable to the age group of 51 to 55 years is "11".

sentences.text: 14. In order to prove the avocation and income of the deceased, the petitioners have not produced any documents.

Therefore, in the absence of satisfactory documents in proof of the income of the deceased, this tribunal has to go by the Lok-Adalath chart, according to which the notional income in relation to the accident of the year 2024 to be taken as Rs.16,500/- p.m.

Therefore, this tribunal assessed the monthly income of petitioner is at Rs.16,500/-.
15.
In the case on hand, undoubtedly the petitioner No.1 is the husband and petitioners No.2 to 4 are the son and daughters of the deceased and they are the dependents on the earnings of the deceased.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in (2017) 16 SCC 680 in between National Insurance Co. Ltd., V/s Pranay (SCCH-3) 11 M.V.C.No.2843/2024 Sethi &
Others case, the future prospects or additional income should be added to monthly income of the deceased.

Therefore, considering the materials available on record, this tribunal is of the opinion that since there are four dependents, it is appropriate to deduct 1/4th of the income towards personal and living expenses of the deceased and then his monthly income would be (Rs.18,150 - Rs.4,537) = Rs.13,613/-.

17. The claimant No.1 is the husband and claimants No.2 to 4 are the son and daughters of the deceased.
Therefore, petitioner No.1 is entitled for Rs.48,400/- towards loss of spousal consortium.

In view of the ratio laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in a decision reported in Magma General Insurance Company Ltd., V/s Nanu Ram alias Churu Ram reported in (2018) 18 SCC 130, the petitioners No.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.40,000/- each towards loss of parental consortium and petitioners are entitled for Rs.19,500/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses and transportation of dead body.

On deposit of the award amount with interest, the petitioner No.1 is entitled to get release 70% of the award through E-payment directly to his account by obtaining the bank account details and remaining 30% shall be kept in Fixed Deposit in any Scheduled Bank for a period of three years, in his name.
